  params <- list(
    gc3_targets     = c(35, 45, 70),  # the NEW targets; the median rung is added
    target_group    = "expressed",    # "expressed" | "promoted" - whose median
    min_codon_prop  = 0.08,           # drop codons used less than this within AA
    max_homopolymer = 6,              # longest run of one base allowed
    gs_repeats      = 3,              # GGGGS units in the linker upstream of P2A
    gs_max_repeat   = 6,              # longest exact repeat allowed inside it
    gs_max_homopolymer = 4,           # tighter homopolymer cap inside it
    seed            = 9               # project standard
  )
}

# Overview

`08_` built a four-rung eGFP **copy-number** ladder: length varies, composition
is held at the expressed-transcriptome GC3 median. This notebook holds the
construct fixed at the **single-eGFP** rung and varies the other axis instead.
One reporter, four synonymous variants, four GC3 levels.

**What "variant" means here.** All four encode the identical 307-residue
protein - HiBiT, (GGGGS)x3, P2A, 1xFLAG, the Waldo linker, one eGFP - and all
four are 921 nt. They differ only in which synonymous codon sits at each
recodable position. Nothing about the construct's parts, order or length
changes; a variant is a different spelling of the same protein.

**Only the parts `08_` already recodes are touched.** Of the construct's 307
codons, **43 are fixed and 264 are free**:

| block | codons | status |
|---|---|---|
| initiator ATG | 1 | fixed |
| HiBiT | 11 | fixed - the published 11-mer, kept bit-identical |
| (GGGGS)x3 linker | 15 | **free** |
| P2A | 19 | fixed - the skipping peptide, kept bit-identical |
| 1xFLAG | 8 | **free** |
| Waldo linker | 12 | fixed - carries the single EcoRI site the cloning needs |
| eGFP | 241 | **free** |

The fixed 42 non-initiator codons sit at GC3 64.3% and cannot move, so every
target is reached by the 264 free ones alone. That is the whole constraint: at
the low end the free codons have to pull the construct down past a GC3-rich
fixed core, and at the high end they are already most of the way there.

**The targets.** `35 / 45 / 57 / 70`. The 57 rung is the expressed-transcriptome
median and is **not drawn again** - it is `08_`'s existing single-eGFP construct,
reproduced here bit-for-bit as a gate (section 6) and then used as exported. The
other three are new. 45 sits just below the eIF3d hypoxia-promoted median
(50.0%), 35 and 70 reach into the tails without leaving the range real mRNAs
occupy.

**Why not wider.** Measured on this protein under the 8% rare-codon floor, the
construct can reach GC3 **11.1% to 95.1%**. Feasibility is not the binding
constraint - codon realism is. Past roughly 30% and 75% the recoder is forced
onto codons that are rare in MDA-MB-231, and the variant stops being "a typical
mRNA that differs in GC3" and becomes "an mRNA with unusual codons". Section 10
measures that drift per variant rather than asserting it is small.

**One recoder, not two.** The machinery lives in `recoder.R`, ported from
section 5 of `08_` with the GC3 target made an argument. `08_` is the design of
record and keeps its inline copy untouched; section 6 here gates the port by
rebuilding `08_`'s single-eGFP construct and asserting it is **bit-identical** to
the exported one. A port that drifted would fail that gate rather than quietly
produce a different ladder.

# 1. Load Libraries

```{r load_libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(readxl)
library(GenomicFeatures)
library(BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38)
library(Biostrings)

source(here("code", "cds_reporter_design", "reporter_helpers.R"))
source(here("code", "cds_reporter_design", "recoder.R"))
```

```{r params_chunk}
lfc_cutoff  <- 0.5
padj_cutoff <- 0.05

run_tag <- paste0("gc3series_", params$target_group)

stopifnot(
  "gc3_targets must hold at least two targets" = length(params$gc3_targets) >= 2,
  "gc3_targets must be percentages in (0, 100)" =
    all(params$gc3_targets > 0 & params$gc3_targets < 100),
  "gc3_targets must be distinct" = !any(duplicated(params$gc3_targets)),
  "target_group must be 'expressed' or 'promoted'" =
    params$target_group %in% c("expressed", "promoted"),
  # A floor above 1/6 would empty the 6-fold families, since their most-used
  # codon can sit only slightly above 1/6.
  "min_codon_prop must be in (0, 1/6)" =
    params$min_codon_prop > 0 && params$min_codon_prop < 1 / 6,
  "max_homopolymer must be at least 4" = params$max_homopolymer >= 4,
  "gs_repeats must be at least 2 for the repeat checks to mean anything" =
    params$gs_repeats >= 2,
  "gs_max_repeat must be below the 15 nt GGGGS unit length" =
    params$gs_max_repeat >= 3 && params$gs_max_repeat < 15,
  "gs_max_homopolymer must not exceed the construct-wide cap" =
    params$gs_max_homopolymer >= 4 &&
    params$gs_max_homopolymer <= params$max_homopolymer
)
cat("GC3 targets (new):", paste(params$gc3_targets, collapse = ", "),
    "| target_group =", params$target_group,
    "| seed =", params$seed, "\n")
```

# 2. Import and Verify the Parts

Identical import and verification to `08_`, on the same spreadsheet. It is
repeated rather than inherited because this notebook must be able to fail on a
changed part file on its own, and because the fixed/free split above is only
meaningful if each part is the sequence it claims to be.

```{r read_parts}
parts_xlsx <- here("accessories", "cds seq.xlsx")
stopifnot("accessories/cds seq.xlsx not found" = file.exists(parts_xlsx))

parts_tbl <- read_excel(parts_xlsx)
names(parts_tbl)[1] <- "construct"

parts <- parts_tbl %>%
  filter(!is.na(construct), !is.na(cds)) %>%
  transmute(part = tolower(str_trim(construct)),
            seq  = toupper(gsub("\\s", "", cds)))
stopifnot("Duplicate part names in cds seq.xlsx" = !any(duplicated(parts$part)))
pseq <- setNames(parts$seq, parts$part)

needed <- c("hibit", "p2a", "flag3x", "egfp", "waldo linker")
stopifnot(
  "A required part is missing from cds seq.xlsx" = all(needed %in% names(pseq)),
  "A part contains non-ACGT characters" = all(!grepl("[^ACGT]", pseq[needed])),
  "A part is not divisible by 3" = all(nchar(pseq[needed]) %% 3 == 0)
)

p2a    <- pseq[["p2a"]]
flag3x <- pseq[["flag3x"]]
egfp   <- pseq[["egfp"]]
waldo  <- pseq[["waldo linker"]]

# The spreadsheet's `hibit` row is the bare 11-residue peptide with no
# initiator. This construct puts it at the N terminus of the ORF, so the
# initiator is prepended here - a design decision rather than a transcription,
# asserted below on both length and translated product.
hibit   <- pseq[["hibit"]]
hibit_n <- paste0("ATG", hibit)

HIBIT_AA  <- "VSGWRLFKKIS"
P2A_AA    <- "ATNFSLLKQAGDVEENPGP"
FLAG_AA   <- "DYKDDDDK"
FLAG3X_AA <- "DYKDHDGDYKDHDIDYKDDDDK"
WALDO_AA  <- "GSAGSAAGSGEF"

aa_of <- function(s) as.character(translate(DNAString(s)))
rc_aa <- function(s) as.character(translate(reverseComplement(DNAString(s))))

flag1x  <- substr(flag3x, 43, 66)
EGFP_AA <- aa_of(egfp)

stopifnot(
  "hibit does not encode the 11-residue HiBiT peptide" = aa_of(hibit) == HIBIT_AA,
  "hibit is not 33 nt" = nchar(hibit) == 33,
  "hibit_n is not the initiator plus HiBiT" =
    nchar(hibit_n) == 36 && aa_of(hibit_n) == paste0("M", HIBIT_AA) &&
    substr(hibit_n, 1, 3) == "ATG" && endsWith(hibit_n, hibit),
  # The spreadsheet carries SmBiT as well, and the two peptides are both 11
  # residues. Reading the wrong row would give a construct that is the right
  # length, in frame, stop-free and entirely wrong.
  "the HiBiT row encodes the SmBiT peptide: the wrong row was read" =
    aa_of(hibit) != "VTGYRLFEEIL",
  "p2a does not encode the expected 19-aa P2A peptide" = aa_of(p2a) == P2A_AA,
  "flag3x does not encode the canonical 3xFLAG peptide" = aa_of(flag3x) == FLAG3X_AA,
  "1xFLAG is not the 24 nt C-terminal repeat of flag3x" =
    nchar(flag1x) == 24 && endsWith(flag3x, flag1x),
  "1xFLAG does not encode the DYKDDDDK epitope" = aa_of(flag1x) == FLAG_AA,
  "egfp is not 723 nt"           = nchar(egfp) == 723,
  "egfp does not start with ATG" = substr(egfp, 1, 3) == "ATG",
  # The GFP chromophore. avGFP numbers it T65-Y66-G67, but eGFP carries an extra
  # Val at position 2, so it sits at 66-68 here. TYG also occurs at residue 39,
  # so a motif-presence check would pass on a sequence with no chromophore.
  "egfp protein does not carry the TYG chromophore at residues 66-68" =
    substr(EGFP_AA, 66, 68) == "TYG",
  "egfp chromophore is not in the expected LTYGVQCF context" =
    substr(EGFP_AA, 65, 72) == "LTYGVQCF",
  "waldo linker is not 36 nt" = nchar(waldo) == 36,
  "waldo linker does not encode GSAGSAAGSGEF" = aa_of(waldo) == WALDO_AA,
  "waldo linker does not end with an in-frame GAATTC EcoRI site" =
    endsWith(waldo, "GAATTC") && (nchar(waldo) - 6) %% 3 == 0
)

# A sequence can be in frame, the right length, and still be backwards, so each
# orientation check is paired with the assertion that the reverse complement
# does NOT encode the same peptide.
stopifnot(
  "Both orientations encode HiBiT: the check is not discriminative" =
    rc_aa(hibit_n) != paste0("M", HIBIT_AA),
  "Both orientations encode P2A: the check is not discriminative" =
    rc_aa(p2a) != P2A_AA,
  "Both orientations encode eGFP: the check is not discriminative" =
    rc_aa(egfp) != EGFP_AA
)
stopifnot("A part carries a stop codon" =
            !any(map_lgl(list(hibit_n, p2a, flag1x, egfp, waldo),
                         ~ any(codon_split(.x) %in% STOP_CODONS))))
cat("Parts verified.\n")
```

# 3. MDA-MB-231 Background and the Median Target

The background the variants are plotted against, and the median rung's target,
are **computed from the same transcript set the density panels draw** - never
typed in. This is the same derivation as `08_` section 3.

```{r load_promotes}
te_hyp <- read_csv(
  here("output", "translation_categories_si3d_vs_sictrl_hypoxia_1hr.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE)

# Direction check. These files hold the sictrl_vs_si3d coefficient despite the
# filename stating the ratio the other way round, so positive te_lfc = eIF3d
# promotes. EIF3D's own rna_lfc must be strongly positive because the siRNA
# depletes its target.
eif3d_rna <- te_hyp %>% filter(symbol == "EIF3D") %>% pull(rna_lfc)
stopifnot("EIF3D rna_lfc is not strongly positive: contrast direction may be flipped" =
            length(eif3d_rna) == 1 && eif3d_rna > 2)
cat("Direction check - EIF3D rna_lfc:", round(eif3d_rna, 2), "\n")

promotes <- te_hyp %>%
  filter(te_lfc > lfc_cutoff, te_padj < padj_cutoff) %>%
  mutate(gene_id_clean = sub("\\..*", "", gene_id))
stopifnot("Expected 1604 eIF3d hypoxia-promoted genes" = nrow(promotes) == 1604)
```

```{r transcripts}
fm <- readRDS(here("output", "predictive_modeling",
                   "feature_matrix_external_stability.rds"))
tx_all      <- fm %>% dplyr::select(transcript_id_clean, gene_id_clean, symbol)
tx_promotes <- tx_all %>% filter(gene_id_clean %in% promotes$gene_id_clean)

missing_gene_ids <- promotes$gene_id_clean[
  !promotes$gene_id_clean %in% tx_all$gene_id_clean]

tx_map <- read_tsv(
  here("accessories", "human", "tx2gene_hs_dm_v49_r111.tsv.gz"),
  col_names = c("transcript_id", "gene_id"), col_types = "cc") %>%
  filter(str_starts(transcript_id, "ENST")) %>%
  transmute(transcript_id_clean = sub("\\..*", "", transcript_id),
            gene_id_clean       = sub("\\..*", "", gene_id))

hyp_samples <- c("NM2025_0094", "NM2025_0095", "NM2025_0096")
hyp_files   <- setNames(
  file.path(here("2025_MDAcells_riboseq", "salmon"), hyp_samples, "quant.sf.gz"),
  hyp_samples)
stopifnot("Hypoxia siCTRL quant files missing" = all(file.exists(hyp_files)))

extra_tx_df <- map_dfr(names(hyp_files), function(s) {
  read_tsv(hyp_files[[s]], col_types = "cdddd",
           col_names = c("Name", "Length", "EffectiveLength", "TPM", "NumReads"),
           skip = 1) %>% dplyr::select(Name, TPM)
}) %>%
  group_by(Name) %>% summarise(mean_tpm = mean(TPM), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(transcript_id_clean = sub("\\..*", "", Name)) %>%
  inner_join(tx_map, by = "transcript_id_clean") %>%
  filter(gene_id_clean %in% missing_gene_ids, mean_tpm > 0) %>%
  group_by(gene_id_clean) %>%
  dplyr::slice_max(mean_tpm, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(promotes %>% dplyr::select(gene_id_clean, symbol) %>% distinct(),
            by = "gene_id_clean") %>%
  dplyr::select(transcript_id_clean, gene_id_clean, symbol)

tx_promotes <- bind_rows(tx_promotes, extra_tx_df)
```

```{r build_metrics}
# One extraction, used for both the metrics and the codon usage table in
# section 4, so the target and the usage describe the same transcripts.
cds_seqs    <- build_cds_seqs(here("accessories", "human", "txdb.gencode49.sqlite"))
cds_int     <- DNAStringSet(trim_internal(as.character(cds_seqs)))
names(cds_int) <- names(cds_seqs)

cds_nostop  <- subseq(cds_seqs, start = 1L,
                      end = BiocGenerics::width(cds_seqs) - 3L)
metrics_all <- tibble(
  transcript_id_clean = names(cds_seqs),
  cds_length = BiocGenerics::width(cds_nostop),
  gc_pct  = as.numeric(letterFrequency(cds_nostop, letters = "GC",
                                       as.prob = TRUE)) * 100,
  gc3_pct = sapply(as.character(cds_int), compute_gc3_pct, USE.NAMES = FALSE)
)
stopifnot("Internal CDS lost frame" =
            all(BiocGenerics::width(cds_int) %% 3 == 0))

expressed <- tx_all %>%
  inner_join(metrics_all, by = "transcript_id_clean") %>% filter(cds_length > 0)
promoted <- tx_promotes %>%
  inner_join(metrics_all, by = "transcript_id_clean") %>% filter(cds_length > 0)

cat("Expressed transcriptome - valid CDS:", nrow(expressed), "\n")
cat("eIF3d promoted        - valid CDS:", nrow(promoted), "\n")

stopifnot(
  "GC% out of range"  = all(expressed$gc_pct  >= 0 & expressed$gc_pct  <= 100),
  "GC3% out of range" = all(expressed$gc3_pct >= 0 & expressed$gc3_pct <= 100),
  "GC3 median not in expected range [40, 65]" =
    between(median(expressed$gc3_pct), 40, 65)
)

actb <- expressed %>% filter(symbol == "ACTB") %>% dplyr::slice(1)
stopifnot("ACTB CDS GC% outside expected 50-70%" = between(actb$gc_pct, 50, 70))
cat("ACTB CDS GC%:", round(actb$gc_pct, 2),
    "| GC3%:", round(actb$gc3_pct, 2), "\n")
```

```{r target}
target_df  <- if (params$target_group == "expressed") expressed else promoted
MEDIAN_GC3 <- median(target_df$gc3_pct)

cat(sprintf("Median rung target from the %s group (n = %s): GC3 %.2f%%\n",
            params$target_group, fmt_n(nrow(target_df)), MEDIAN_GC3))

# The new targets must not collide with the median rung, which is imported
# rather than drawn: two rungs at the same target would be two spellings of the
# same specification and would make the series' labels ambiguous.
stopifnot(
  "A new GC3 target coincides with the median rung" =
    all(abs(params$gc3_targets - MEDIAN_GC3) > 0.5)
)
```

# 4. Codon Usage of the Expressed Transcriptome

Each position needs a real codon, not just a third-base class. The choice is
weighted by the pooled synonymous usage of the **same expressed transcripts**
that set the median target, computed here rather than taken from a published
table. The usage weights do **not** change between variants - only the
third-base target does - so a difference between variants is a difference in
GC3, not in which codon table they were drawn from.

```{r codon_usage}
GEN <- GENETIC_CODE
# as.character() drops the codon names and every lookup below indexes by codon,
# so they are restored explicitly: without them a lookup silently returns NA.
AA <- setNames(as.character(GEN), names(GEN))
stopifnot("Codon-to-amino-acid lookup lost its names" =
            identical(names(AA), names(GEN)))

sense <- names(GEN)[AA != "*"]

expr_seqs <- cds_int[names(cds_int) %in% expressed$transcript_id_clean]
stopifnot("Expressed CDS subset is empty" = length(expr_seqs) > 0)

cf <- trinucleotideFrequency(expr_seqs, step = 3)
stopifnot("trinucleotideFrequency lost its codon column names" =
            !is.null(colnames(cf)) && all(names(GEN) %in% colnames(cf)))

usage <- tibble(codon = colnames(cf), count = colSums(cf)) %>%
  filter(AA[codon] != "*") %>%
  mutate(aa = AA[codon]) %>%
  group_by(aa) %>% mutate(prop = count / sum(count)) %>% ungroup()

stopifnot(
  "Synonymous proportions do not sum to 1 within every amino acid" =
    all(abs((usage %>% group_by(aa) %>% summarise(s = sum(prop)))$s - 1) < 1e-9),
  "A sense codon is missing from the usage table" = setequal(usage$codon, sense)
)

# Biological spot-check: CTG is the dominant Leu codon in human.
leu <- usage %>% filter(aa == "L") %>% dplyr::slice_max(prop, n = 1)
stopifnot("CTG is not the most-used Leu codon: usage table may be misaligned" =
            leu$codon == "CTG")
cat("CTG share of Leu codons:", round(100 * leu$prop, 1), "%\n")

USE   <- setNames(usage$prop, usage$codon)
BASES <- c("A", "C", "G", "T")

pick_list <- function(cods) {
  keep <- cods[USE[cods] >= params$min_codon_prop]
  if (!length(keep)) cods[which.max(USE[cods])] else keep
}
MENU <- map(split(sense, AA[sense]), function(cods) {
  by_base <- map(setNames(BASES, BASES), ~ cods[str_sub(cods, 3, 3) == .x])
  map(by_base[lengths(by_base) > 0], pick_list)
})
AVAIL <- map(MENU, names)
```

```{r base_ratios}
# Per-transcript third-base percentages, the same matrix section 9 reports
# against. R_G and R_A are the within-class splits and are held CONSTANT across
# every GC3 target: a variant changes how many third bases are G or C, not how
# the G/C and A/T classes are divided internally. Letting them float per target
# would confound GC3 with a second compositional change.
b3_col  <- str_sub(colnames(cf), 3, 3)
tx_n3   <- sapply(setNames(BASES, BASES),
                  function(b) rowSums(cf[, b3_col == b, drop = FALSE]))
tx_pct3 <- 100 * tx_n3 / rowSums(tx_n3)

med3 <- apply(tx_pct3, 2, median)
R_G <- med3[["G"]] / (med3[["G"]] + med3[["C"]])   # share of GC-enders that are G
R_A <- med3[["A"]] / (med3[["A"]] + med3[["T"]])   # share of AT-enders that are A

stopifnot(
  "Per-transcript third-base percentages do not sum to 100" =
    all(abs(rowSums(tx_pct3) - 100) < 1e-9),
  "Third-base split ratios are out of range" =
    between(R_G, 0, 1) && between(R_A, 0, 1),
  # The ratios and MEDIAN_GC3 must come from the same statistic, or the median
  # rung's target is two populations stitched together. This holds for the
  # median rung only; the other targets deliberately depart from it, which is
  # what the series is.
  "Split ratios and the median GC3 disagree: they are not the same statistic" =
    abs((med3[["G"]] + med3[["C"]]) / sum(med3) * 100 - MEDIAN_GC3) < 1
)

cat("Expressed transcriptome, per-transcript median third base:",
    paste(sprintf("%s %.1f%%", BASES, med3), collapse = "  "), "\n")
cat(sprintf("G:(G+C) = %.3f   A:(A+T) = %.3f (held fixed across targets)\n",
            R_G, R_A))
```

# 5. How Far This Protein Can Go

The reachable GC3 range, measured rather than assumed, before any variant is
drawn. It is what makes "35 and 70 are inside the feasible range" a statement
about this construct instead of a guess.

```{r feasible_range}
hibit_cv <- codon_split(hibit_n)
p2a_cv   <- codon_split(p2a)
waldo_cv <- codon_split(waldo)
flag_cv  <- codon_split(flag1x)
egfp_cv  <- codon_split(egfp)

GS_UNIT_AA <- "GGGGS"
GS_UNIT_NT <- 3L * nchar(GS_UNIT_AA)
gs_aa      <- strrep(GS_UNIT_AA, params$gs_repeats)
gs_naive   <- naive_encoding(gs_aa, usage)
gs_cv      <- codon_split(gs_naive)
n_gs       <- length(gs_cv)

# The free codons, in the order they sit in the construct.
free_aa <- AA[c(gs_cv, flag_cv, egfp_cv)]
fixed_cv <- c(hibit_cv, p2a_cv, waldo_cv)
n_total  <- length(c(hibit_cv, gs_cv, p2a_cv, flag_cv, waldo_cv, egfp_cv))

stopifnot(
  "Construct is not 307 codons" = n_total == 307,
  "Free/fixed codon counts do not add up" =
    length(free_aa) + length(fixed_cv) == n_total
)

# A free position can end G/C if any menu codon does, and MUST end G/C if every
# menu codon does. Summing those over the free positions, plus the fixed core,
# gives the construct's floor and ceiling on the internal basis.
can_gc  <- map_lgl(MENU[free_aa], ~ any(names(.x) %in% c("G", "C")))
must_gc <- map_lgl(MENU[free_aa], ~ all(names(.x) %in% c("G", "C")))

fixed_gc3_n <- sum(str_sub(fixed_cv[-1], 3, 3) %in% c("G", "C"))
basis_n     <- n_total - 1L   # the initiator is excluded, as in block_needs

gc3_floor   <- 100 * (fixed_gc3_n + sum(must_gc)) / basis_n
gc3_ceiling <- 100 * (fixed_gc3_n + sum(can_gc))  / basis_n

cat(sprintf("Fixed core: %d of %d non-initiator codons, GC3 %.1f%%\n",
            length(fixed_cv) - 1L, basis_n,
            100 * fixed_gc3_n / (length(fixed_cv) - 1L)))
cat(sprintf("Construct GC3 reachable range: %.1f%% to %.1f%%\n",
            gc3_floor, gc3_ceiling))

stopifnot(
  "A requested GC3 target is outside what this protein can reach" =
    all(params$gc3_targets > gc3_floor & params$gc3_targets < gc3_ceiling),
  "The median rung's target is outside the reachable range" =
    MEDIAN_GC3 > gc3_floor && MEDIAN_GC3 < gc3_ceiling
)
```

# 6. Gate: the Port Reproduces `08_`

`recoder.R` is a port. Before it is trusted to draw three new variants, it has
to rebuild the one construct whose answer is already known. This runs the same
two-stage build `08_` does - the GS linker and FLAG together, then the eGFP
copy - at the **median** target, and asserts the result is bit-identical to the
exported single-eGFP sequence.

The RNG makes this a strict test rather than a loose one: `08_` seeds once at
the start of its ladder and the single-eGFP rung is the second draw, so an
identical sequence means identical third-base assignments, identical codon
sampling and an identical number of rejected draws. A port that changed the
order of a single `sample()` call would fail here.

```{r build_fn}
# What a drawn GS linker has to satisfy on top of the construct-wide motif
# checks. Pairwise-distinct units is implied by the repeat bound, but it is the
# constraint the design is actually about, so it is stated rather than inferred.
gs_units <- function(linker)
  substring(linker,
            seq(1L, by = GS_UNIT_NT, length.out = params$gs_repeats),
            seq(GS_UNIT_NT, by = GS_UNIT_NT, length.out = params$gs_repeats))

longest_homopolymer <- function(s)
  max(nchar(str_extract_all(s, "(A+|C+|G+|T+)")[[1]]))

gs_ok <- function(block) {
  linker <- paste0(block[seq_len(n_gs)], collapse = "")
  anyDuplicated(gs_units(linker)) == 0L &&
    max_internal_repeat(linker) <= params$gs_max_repeat &&
    longest_homopolymer(linker) <= params$gs_max_homopolymer
}

# Glycine's only G-ending codon is GGG, and inside a polyglycine run it is
# always followed by another GG, so picking it puts a 5 nt G run in the linker.
# The construct-wide menu cannot say "not here", so the linker's glycine
# positions give up G and the G-ending codons the target needs go to the
# linker's serines (TCG) or FLAG's lysines (AAG) instead.
gs_menus   <- map(MENU[AA[gs_cv]], function(m)
  if (identical(m[["G"]], "GGG")) m[names(m) != "G"] else m)
free_menus <- c(gs_menus, MENU[AA[flag_cv]])
stopifnot("The GS menu restriction did not remove GGG" =
            !any(map_lgl(gs_menus, ~ "GGG" %in% unlist(.x))))

# A `need` vector built from a chosen GC count, keeping the transcriptome's
# within-class splits. Used only by the fallback below; the primary path takes
# its need from `block_needs`, exactly as `08_` does.
needs_from_ngc <- function(n_block, n_gc) {
  n_at <- n_block - n_gc
  g <- round(n_gc * R_G); a <- round(n_at * R_A)
  c(A = a, C = n_gc - g, G = g, T = n_at - a)[BASES]
}

# Build the single-eGFP construct at one GC3 target, in the two stages `08_`
# uses. Returns the assembled codon vector plus the two recoded blocks, so the
# per-part panels later can report each part on its own rather than re-cutting
# the assembled string by coordinates.
#
# Stage 1 draws the GS linker and FLAG as ONE 23-codon assignment rather than
# two blocks, because the third-base target is a count over the whole construct
# and splitting it between them would need an arbitrary allocation.
#
# **Stage 1 can be asked for something the linker cannot encode.** `block_needs`
# hands it the whole construct-wide shortfall, clamped to its 23 codons. At
# GC3 35 that clamp asks for ZERO GC-ending codons out of 23, which restricts
# the linker's 12 glycines to GGA and GGT - two codons sharing GG, from which no
# 45 nt arrangement satisfies the 6 nt internal-repeat bound. The draw then
# fails after thousands of attempts rather than returning a repetitive linker,
# which is the right failure but not a usable one.
#
# So stage 1 asks for its `block_needs` share first and, when no clean draw
# exists, walks outward to neighbouring GC counts and takes the first that does.
# The construct still lands on target: stage 2's `need` is recomputed against
# the prefix ACTUALLY built, and eGFP's 241 codons have ample room to absorb
# whatever the 23 gave up. What is given up is only the claim that the GS+FLAG
# stretch itself sits at the construct's GC3 - which section 11 reports rather
# than assumes.
#
# The median target reaches a clean draw on the first candidate, so this leaves
# the section 6 gate untouched: the fallback changes nothing unless it fires.
build_variant <- function(target_gc3, seed = params$seed,
                          max_try0 = 5000, max_try_alt = 2000) {
  R <- make_recoder(target_gc3, R_G, R_A, MENU, USE, AA, params$max_homopolymer)
  set.seed(seed)

  n_block <- length(c(gs_cv, flag_cv))
  need0   <- R$block_needs(n_block, c(hibit_cv, p2a_cv))
  n_gc0   <- need0[["G"]] + need0[["C"]]
  n_g_cap <- sum(map_lgl(free_menus, ~ "G" %in% names(.x)))

  # Candidate GC counts, nearest to the block_needs share first.
  cand <- c(n_gc0, n_gc0 + unlist(map(seq_len(n_block), ~ c(.x, -.x))))
  cand <- cand[cand >= 0 & cand <= n_block]

  drawn0 <- NULL; n_gc_used <- NA_integer_
  for (g in cand) {
    nd <- if (g == n_gc0) need0 else needs_from_ngc(n_block, g)
    # Dropping GGG from the linker's glycines caps how many G-enders exist.
    if (nd[["G"]] > n_g_cap) next
    drawn0 <- tryCatch(
      R$draw_clean_block(
        c(gs_cv, flag_cv), nd,
        assemble  = function(b) c(hibit_cv, b[seq_len(n_gs)], p2a_cv,
                                  b[-seq_len(n_gs)]),
        n_linkers = 0, extra_ok = gs_ok, menus = free_menus,
        max_try   = if (g == n_gc0) max_try0 else max_try_alt),
      error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(drawn0)) { need0 <- nd; n_gc_used <- g; break }
  }
  stopifnot(
    "No clean GS+FLAG draw exists at any GC count for this target" =
      !is.null(drawn0)
  )

  gs_new   <- drawn0$block[seq_len(n_gs)]
  flag_new <- drawn0$block[-seq_len(n_gs)]
  prefix   <- c(hibit_cv, gs_new, p2a_cv, flag_new, waldo_cv)

  need1  <- R$block_needs(length(egfp_cv), prefix)
  drawn1 <- R$draw_clean_block(egfp_cv, need1,
                               assemble = function(b) c(prefix, b),
                               n_linkers = 1)

  cat(sprintf("  target %.1f%%: GS+FLAG %d GC-enders of %d (block_needs asked %d%s), draw %d; ",
              target_gc3, n_gc_used, n_block, n_gc0,
              if (n_gc_used == n_gc0) "" else " - FALLBACK", drawn0$tries))
  cat(sprintf("eGFP need A %d C %d G %d T %d, draw %d\n",
              need1[["A"]], need1[["C"]], need1[["G"]], need1[["T"]],
              drawn1$tries))

  list(cv        = c(prefix, drawn1$block),
       gs        = paste0(gs_new,       collapse = ""),
       flag      = paste0(flag_new,     collapse = ""),
       egfp      = paste0(drawn1$block, collapse = ""),
       n_gc_used = n_gc_used,
       n_gc_ask  = n_gc0)
}
```

```{r gate_reproduce_08}
ref_path <- here("output", "cds_reporter_design",
                 "08_recoded_assembled_sequences_upto3x_expressed.csv")
stopifnot(
  "08_ has not been knit: its exported sequences are missing. Run 08_ first." =
    file.exists(ref_path)
)
ref08 <- read_csv(ref_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>% filter(gfp_copies == 1)
stopifnot("08_'s export has no single-eGFP rung" = nrow(ref08) == 1)

cat("Rebuilding 08_'s single-eGFP construct at the median target:\n")
median_rebuild <- build_variant(MEDIAN_GC3)
median_seq     <- paste0(median_rebuild$cv, collapse = "")

stopifnot(
  "The ported recoder does NOT reproduce 08_'s single-eGFP construct" =
    identical(median_seq, ref08$cds[[1]]),
  "Rebuilt construct is not 921 nt" = nchar(median_seq) == 921
)
cat("Gate passed: the port reproduces 08_'s 921 nt construct bit-for-bit.\n")

# Discriminative companion. A gate that can only pass is not a gate: the same
# comparison must FAIL on a construct drawn at a different target, or it would
# be testing that two strings exist rather than that they agree.
probe <- paste0(build_variant(MEDIAN_GC3 - 10)$cv, collapse = "")
stopifnot(
  "A 10-point-lower target reproduces the same sequence: the gate is not discriminative" =
    !identical(probe, ref08$cds[[1]]),
  "The probe changed the protein, so it is the wrong companion" =
    aa_of(probe) == aa_of(median_seq)
)
cat("Companion check: a construct drawn 10 points lower differs, as it must.\n")
```

# 7. Build the Series

Three new variants, each an independent build from the same seed at its own
target. The median rung is `08_`'s exported sequence, used as it stands.

```{r build_series}
cat("Drawing the new variants:\n")
new_variants <- map(set_names(params$gc3_targets,
                              sprintf("%g", params$gc3_targets)),
                    build_variant)

# The median rung enters from 08_'s export rather than from `median_rebuild`.
# They are bit-identical - section 6 asserted exactly that - so this is about
# provenance: the mid rung of this series IS the construct already reviewed and
# built elsewhere, not a copy this notebook happened to redraw.
median_variant     <- median_rebuild
median_variant$cv  <- codon_split(ref08$cds[[1]])

variants <- c(new_variants, list(median_variant))
targets  <- c(params$gc3_targets, MEDIAN_GC3)
ord      <- order(targets)
variants <- variants[ord]
targets  <- targets[ord]
is_median <- abs(targets - MEDIAN_GC3) < 1e-9

names(variants) <- sprintf("HiBiT-GS-P2A-FLAG-link-1xeGFP GC3 %.0f%%",
                           targets)
stopifnot("Two variants share a name" = !any(duplicated(names(variants))))

seqs <- map_chr(variants, ~ paste0(.x$cv, collapse = ""))

cat("\nSeries built:\n")
walk2(names(variants), seqs, ~ cat(sprintf("  %-46s %d nt, GC3 %.1f%%\n",
                                           .x, nchar(.y),
                                           compute_gc3_pct(.y))))
```

# 8. Validation

A synonymous series is only legitimate if the protein is untouched and every
variant is genuinely a different spelling. Both are measured on DNA translated
independently, not on the bookkeeping that produced it.

```{r validate_protein}
# The protein every variant must encode, assembled from the imported parts.
expected_aa <- aa_of(paste0(hibit_n, gs_naive, p2a, flag1x, waldo, egfp))

walk2(names(seqs), seqs, function(nm, s) {
  stopifnot(
    "A variant is not 921 nt" = nchar(s) == 921,
    "A variant lost frame"    = nchar(s) %% 3 == 0,
    "A variant changed the protein" = aa_of(s) == expected_aa,
    "A variant carries an internal stop codon" =
      !any(codon_split(s) %in% STOP_CODONS),
    "A variant does not begin with the initiator" = substr(s, 1, 3) == "ATG"
  )
})
cat("All", length(seqs), "variants: 921 nt, in frame, stop-free,",
    "identical", nchar(expected_aa), "residue protein\n")

# The fixed blocks must be bit-identical across the series, which is the
# notebook's central claim - only the already-recoded parts changed.
walk2(names(seqs), seqs, function(nm, s) {
  cv <- codon_split(s)
  stopifnot(
    "HiBiT is not bit-identical across variants" =
      paste0(cv[seq_along(hibit_cv)], collapse = "") == hibit_n,
    "P2A is not bit-identical across variants" =
      paste0(cv[length(hibit_cv) + n_gs + seq_along(p2a_cv)],
             collapse = "") == p2a,
    "The Waldo linker is not bit-identical across variants" =
      paste0(cv[length(hibit_cv) + n_gs + length(p2a_cv) + length(flag_cv) +
                  seq_along(waldo_cv)], collapse = "") == waldo
  )
})
cat("Fixed blocks (HiBiT, P2A, Waldo linker) bit-identical in every variant\n")

# Discriminative companion: the FREE blocks must NOT be identical across
# variants, or the series is four copies of one construct under four labels.
stopifnot(
  "Two variants are the same sequence: the series has no spread" =
    !any(duplicated(seqs)),
  "The recoded eGFP blocks are identical across variants" =
    !any(duplicated(map_chr(variants, "egfp")))
)
cat("eGFP differs between every pair of variants, as it must\n")

# The GS+FLAG stretch is a different matter, and two variants COULD share it.
# It is 23 codons drawn from one seed, so two targets that end up asking it for
# the same number of GC-enders would get the same draw. That nearly happens at
# 35 and 45, which both land on 2 GC-enders and therefore show identical
# per-part GC and GC3 in section 11 - but the sequences still differ, because
# the 35 variant reaches 2 through the fallback, having already spent 5,000
# rejected draws on the count `block_needs` asked for, so its RNG state differs
# when the accepted draw is made.
#
# That makes per-part composition an unreliable way to tell these apart, which
# is the reason this check compares SEQUENCES rather than reading the numbers
# off section 11. If a future target did produce a genuinely shared stretch it
# would not be a defect - construct-wide GC3 would still separate the variants,
# and eGFP is 241 of the 264 free codons - but a reader comparing two sequences
# by eye would see an identical 69 nt run and suspect one, so it is named.
# Checked per part, not on the concatenation: FLAG is 8 codons of D/Y/K, and at
# GC3 0 every one of them has a single AT-ending codon (GAT, TAT, AAA), so a
# FLAG drawn at 0% is not one encoding among many - it is the ONLY one. Any two
# variants whose FLAG lands at 0% therefore share it by arithmetic rather than
# by coincidence, and a check on `paste0(gs, flag)` would miss that whenever the
# GS linker differs.
walk(c("gs", "flag", "egfp"), function(part) {
  v <- map_chr(variants, part)
  dup <- which(duplicated(v) | duplicated(v, fromLast = TRUE))
  if (length(dup)) {
    grp <- split(names(variants)[dup], v[dup])
    walk(grp, ~ cat(sprintf("  %-5s identical in: %s\n", part,
                            paste(.x, collapse = " | "))))
  } else {
    cat(sprintf("  %-5s differs in every variant\n", part))
  }
})
stopifnot(
  # eGFP is the part the series actually turns on; it must never repeat.
  "Two variants share an eGFP block" =
    !any(duplicated(map_chr(variants, "egfp")))
)
```

```{r validate_motifs}
ec <- map_int(seqs, ~ str_count(.x, fixed("GAATTC")))
stopifnot("A variant does not carry exactly one EcoRI site" = all(ec == 1))
cat("Internal EcoRI sites per variant:", paste(ec, collapse = ", "),
    "(one per Waldo linker, as designed)\n")

max_run <- map_int(seqs, ~ max(nchar(str_extract_all(.x, "(A+|C+|G+|T+)")[[1]])))
stopifnot("A variant carries a homopolymer longer than max_homopolymer" =
            all(max_run <= params$max_homopolymer))
cat("Longest homopolymer per variant:", paste(max_run, collapse = ", "),
    "nt (cap", params$max_homopolymer, ")\n")
```

The GS linker is the one part whose constraint is about repeats rather than
composition, so it is checked separately in every variant - and checked against
the naive encoding, which must **fail** the same measures. Without that
companion the repeat bound would pass on a measure that never finds a repeat.

```{r validate_gs_linker}
gs_tbl <- tibble(
  variant   = names(variants),
  seq       = map_chr(variants, "gs"),
  n_units   = map_int(seq, ~ length(unique(gs_units(.x)))),
  repeat_nt = map_int(seq, max_internal_repeat),
  homo_nt   = map_int(seq, longest_homopolymer),
  gc3_pct   = map_dbl(seq, compute_gc3_pct)
)
print(gs_tbl %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 1))) %>%
        as.data.frame())

walk(gs_tbl$seq, function(s) {
  stopifnot(
    "A recoded GS linker changed the peptide" = aa_of(s) == gs_aa,
    "A recoded GS linker changed length" = nchar(s) == nchar(gs_naive),
    "Two GGGGS units in a recoded linker are identical" =
      length(unique(gs_units(s))) == params$gs_repeats,
    "A recoded GS linker still carries a long internal repeat" =
      max_internal_repeat(s) <= params$gs_max_repeat,
    "A recoded GS linker exceeds its homopolymer cap" =
      longest_homopolymer(s) <= params$gs_max_homopolymer
  )
})
stopifnot(
  # Discriminative companions: both measures must fire on the naive encoding.
  # A tandem repeat of n units has a repeated substring of all but the last
  # unit, so that is the bound to expect rather than a guessed number.
  "The repeat measure does not detect the naive tandem repeat" =
    max_internal_repeat(gs_naive) >= nchar(gs_naive) - GS_UNIT_NT,
  "The naive encoding passes the unit-distinctness check: not discriminative" =
    length(unique(gs_units(gs_naive))) < params$gs_repeats
)
cat("GS linker: distinct units and repeat bound hold in every variant;",
    "the naive encoding fails both\n")
```

# 9. Where Each Variant Landed

```{r composition}
comp_tbl <- tibble(
  variant    = names(variants),
  gc3_target = targets,
  source     = ifelse(is_median, "08_ (imported)", "drawn here"),
  cds_length = map_int(seqs, nchar),
  gc_pct     = map_dbl(seqs, orf_gc_pct),
  gc3_pct    = map_dbl(seqs, orf_gc3_pct),
  # Did the GS+FLAG stage get the share block_needs asked for, or did the
  # fallback hold it back so the linker stayed cloneable? Carried into the
  # exported table because it is the one place the two stages differ.
  gs_flag_gc_enders = map_int(variants, ~ as.integer(.x$n_gc_used)),
  gs_flag_gc_asked  = map_int(variants, ~ as.integer(.x$n_gc_ask))
) %>%
  mutate(d_gc3 = gc3_pct - gc3_target,
         stage1 = ifelse(gs_flag_gc_enders == gs_flag_gc_asked,
                         "full share", "fallback"))

print(comp_tbl %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 2))) %>%
        as.data.frame())

stopifnot(
  "A variant missed its GC3 target by more than 1 point" =
    all(abs(comp_tbl$d_gc3) <= 1),
  "The series is not monotone in GC3" =
    !is.unsorted(comp_tbl$gc3_pct),
  "Variants differ in length: the series is not synonymous" =
    length(unique(comp_tbl$cds_length)) == 1
)
cat(sprintf("\nAll %d variants within 1 point of target, all %d nt.\n",
            nrow(comp_tbl), comp_tbl$cds_length[1]))
cat(sprintf("GC3 spread %.1f points; total GC spread %.1f points.\n",
            diff(range(comp_tbl$gc3_pct)), diff(range(comp_tbl$gc_pct))))

fb <- comp_tbl %>% filter(stage1 == "fallback")
if (nrow(fb)) {
  cat(sprintf("Stage-1 fallback fired on %d of %d variants (%s): the GS+FLAG\n",
              nrow(fb), nrow(comp_tbl), paste(sprintf("%.0f%%", fb$gc3_target),
                                              collapse = ", ")))
  cat("  stretch was held back from its full share so the linker stayed",
      "cloneable;\n  eGFP absorbed the remainder. Section 11 shows where",
      "each part landed.\n")
} else {
  cat("Stage-1 fallback did not fire: every variant got its full share.\n")
}
# The median rung must never reach the fallback - if it did, it would no longer
# be the construct section 6 reproduced.
stopifnot("The median rung used the stage-1 fallback" =
            comp_tbl$stage1[is_median] == "full share")
```

**Total GC is not controlled and is not expected to be flat.** Positions 1 and 2
are fixed by the protein, so the only lever is the third base; moving GC3 moves
total GC with it, at roughly a third of the rate. The GC panel in section 10
reports where that lands rather than treating it as a second target.

```{r percentiles}
ref_df  <- comp_tbl %>%
  transmute(reporter = variant, cds_length, gc_pct, gc3_pct)
pct_tbl <- reporter_percentiles(expressed, promoted, ref_df)
print(pct_tbl)
stopifnot("Percentiles must lie in [0, 100]" =
            all(pct_tbl$pct_expressed >= 0 & pct_tbl$pct_expressed <= 100 &
                pct_tbl$pct_promoted  >= 0 & pct_tbl$pct_promoted  <= 100))
```

# 10. Density Panels

The same panel style as `08_`, with one reference line per variant instead of
one per rung. Because every variant is the same length, the length panel would
draw four lines on top of each other and is deliberately omitted.

```{r density_setup}
group_cols <- c("All expressed mRNAs"    = "grey70",
                "eIF3d hypoxia promotes" = "#E69F00")

# A single-hue ramp ordered by GC3, so the legend reads as a series rather than
# as four unrelated constructs. Deliberately the same dark-blue family `07_`
# and `08_` use for reporter reference lines: grey and orange are spoken for by
# the two gene distributions, and the project reserves orange for eIF3d.
variant_cols <- setNames(
  colorRampPalette(c("#A6CEE3", "#0072B2", "#03314D"))(nrow(comp_tbl)),
  comp_tbl$variant)

ref_plot_df <- ref_df %>%
  mutate(color    = unname(variant_cols[reporter]),
         linetype = "solid",
         reporter = factor(reporter, levels = reporter))
```

  expressed, promoted, "gc3_pct",
  xlab    = "CDS GC3 content (%)",
  title   = "CDS GC3 content, MDA-MB-231, single-eGFP HiBiT reporter GC3 series",
  outfile = paste0("cds_reporter_12_density_cds_gc3_", run_tag, ".pdf"),
  luc_tbl = ref_plot_df, group_cols = group_cols)
```

  expressed, promoted, "gc_pct",
  xlab    = "CDS GC content (%)",
  title   = "CDS GC content, MDA-MB-231, single-eGFP HiBiT reporter GC3 series",

  luc_tbl = ref_plot_df, group_cols = group_cols)
```

# 11. Per-Part GC3

The construct-wide number can be met evenly or carried by one part. eGFP is 241
of the 264 free codons, so it will dominate by weight whatever happens - the
question this panel answers is whether the 23-codon GS+FLAG stage is pulling in
the same direction or being overridden. Section 7's fallback makes that a real
question rather than a rhetorical one: at the extreme targets the GS+FLAG stage
is deliberately held back from its full share.

```{r part_bars, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
part_tbl <- tibble(
  variant = rep(names(variants), each = 3),
  part    = rep(c(sprintf("GS linker (%dxGGGGS)", params$gs_repeats),
                  "FLAG (1x)", "eGFP"), times = length(variants)),
  seq     = as.vector(rbind(map_chr(variants, "gs"),
                            map_chr(variants, "flag"),
                            map_chr(variants, "egfp")))
) %>%
  mutate(gc3_pct = map_dbl(seq, compute_gc3_pct),
         gc_pct  = map_dbl(seq, gc_pct_of),
         variant = factor(variant, levels = names(variants)),
         part    = factor(part, levels = unique(part)))

stopifnot(
  "Part GC3 out of range" = all(between(part_tbl$gc3_pct, 0, 100)),
  "Part GC out of range"  = all(between(part_tbl$gc_pct, 0, 100)),
  "A part sequence is missing" = !any(is.na(part_tbl$seq))
)

p_parts <- ggplot(part_tbl, aes(part, gc3_pct, fill = variant)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = MEDIAN_GC3, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = MEDIAN_GC3, label = "expressed median",
           hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.6, size = 3.2, color = "grey30") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = variant_cols, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "GC3 content (%)",
       title = "GC3 by part, single-eGFP HiBiT reporter GC3 series",
       subtitle = sprintf("n = %d variants; expressed median %.1f%%",
                          nrow(comp_tbl), MEDIAN_GC3)) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
print(p_parts)
ggsave(here("plots", paste0("cds_reporter_12_part_gc3_", run_tag, ".pdf")),
       p_parts, width = 9, height = 5)

print(part_tbl %>%
        dplyr::select(variant, part, gc3_pct, gc_pct) %>%
        mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 1))) %>%
        pivot_wider(names_from = part, values_from = c(gc3_pct, gc_pct)) %>%
        as.data.frame())
```

# 12. Codon-Usage Drift

The diagnostic that decides whether an extreme variant is usable. Reaching a GC3
target far from the median means preferring codons the cell uses less, and past
some point the construct stops being a GC3 variant of a typical mRNA and becomes
an mRNA full of rare codons - a confound, since rare codons slow elongation in
their own right.

Two measures, both over the **free codons only** (the fixed core is the same in
every variant and would dilute both):

- **mean synonymous usage** - the average 231 usage proportion of the chosen
  codons. The expressed transcriptome's own value is the reference.
- **worst-case rarity** - the lowest usage proportion drawn, and how many
  positions sit below the `min_codon_prop` floor. A mean can look healthy while
  a handful of positions are terrible.

```{r usage_drift}
free_idx <- c(length(hibit_cv) + seq_len(n_gs),                       # GS linker
              length(hibit_cv) + n_gs + length(p2a_cv) + seq_len(length(flag_cv)),
              length(hibit_cv) + n_gs + length(p2a_cv) + length(flag_cv) +
                length(waldo_cv) + seq_len(length(egfp_cv)))
stopifnot(
  "Free index does not select 264 codons" = length(free_idx) == 264,
  # The free index is built from block lengths, so an off-by-one would still
  # produce 264 entries while pointing at the wrong codons. Anchor it: the
  # fixed blocks must be exactly the positions it leaves out.
  "Free index overlaps a fixed block" =
    !any(free_idx %in% c(seq_along(hibit_cv),
                         length(hibit_cv) + n_gs + seq_along(p2a_cv),
                         length(hibit_cv) + n_gs + length(p2a_cv) +
                           length(flag_cv) + seq_along(waldo_cv)))
)

# Reference: the usage a draw would average if it followed 231 usage exactly,
# i.e. the usage-weighted mean usage within each free position's amino acid.
ref_mean_use <- mean(map_dbl(AA[c(gs_cv, flag_cv, egfp_cv)], function(a) {
  cods <- sense[AA[sense] == a]
  sum(USE[cods] * USE[cods])
}))

drift_tbl <- map2_dfr(names(variants), variants, function(nm, v) {
  free_cods <- v$cv[free_idx]
  u <- USE[free_cods]
  tibble(variant      = nm,
         mean_usage   = mean(u),
         min_usage    = min(u),
         n_below_floor = sum(u < params$min_codon_prop),
         pct_below_floor = 100 * mean(u < params$min_codon_prop))
}) %>%
  mutate(variant = factor(variant, levels = names(variants)),
         gc3_target = targets,
         usage_ratio = mean_usage / ref_mean_use)

print(drift_tbl %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
        as.data.frame())
cat(sprintf("\n231-usage-weighted reference mean usage: %.3f\n", ref_mean_use))

stopifnot(
  "Usage proportions out of range" =
    all(between(drift_tbl$mean_usage, 0, 1) & between(drift_tbl$min_usage, 0, 1)),
  # Positions below the floor can only come from an amino acid whose menu would
  # otherwise have been emptied (pick_list keeps the most-used codon in that
  # case). Anything else means the floor is not being applied.
  "A variant drew codons below the floor at more than 5% of free positions" =
    all(drift_tbl$pct_below_floor <= 5)
)

p_drift <- ggplot(drift_tbl, aes(gc3_target, mean_usage, color = variant)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = ref_mean_use, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = ref_mean_use, label = "231 usage reference",
           hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.6, size = 3.2, color = "grey30") +
  geom_line(aes(group = 1), color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 3.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = variant_cols, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "CDS GC3 target (%)",
       y = "Mean synonymous usage of the recoded codons",
       title = "Codon-usage drift across the GC3 series",
       subtitle = sprintf("free codons only (n = %d of %d); dashed = 231 usage",
                          length(free_idx), n_total)) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
print(p_drift)
ggsave(here("plots", paste0("cds_reporter_12_usage_drift_", run_tag, ".pdf")),
       p_drift, width = 8, height = 5)
```

```{r drift_summary}
worst <- drift_tbl %>% dplyr::slice_min(usage_ratio, n = 1)
cat(sprintf("Least 231-like variant: %s (mean usage %.1f%% of the reference)\n",
            worst$variant, 100 * worst$usage_ratio))
cat("Read this alongside the GC3 panel: a variant that hits its target but sits\n",
    "well below the reference is trading codon realism for composition.\n", sep = "")
```

# 13. Outputs

```{r write_outputs}
outdir <- here("output", "cds_reporter_design")

# Every part of this construct is stop-free, so the assembled ORF has no
# terminator. `cds` stays the SENSE ORF - it is what the GC3 figures, the
# percentiles and section 6's gate against `08_` are all computed on - and
# `cds_ordered` is what gets synthesised: the same sequence plus a terminal
# TAA. The stop goes at the END of the full CDS and nowhere else; one upstream
# of P2A would terminate translation before FLAG and eGFP exist.
ORF_STOP  <- "TAA"
seqs_ordered <- paste0(seqs, ORF_STOP)

stopifnot(
  "A variant already carries a stop codon: appending one would duplicate it" =
    !any(map_lgl(seqs, ~ any(codon_split(.x) %in% STOP_CODONS))),
  "An ordered variant does not end in the terminator" =
    all(map_lgl(seqs_ordered, ~ tail(codon_split(.x), 1) == ORF_STOP)),
  "An ordered variant carries a stop before the end" =
    !any(map_lgl(seqs_ordered,
                 ~ any(head(codon_split(.x), -1) %in% STOP_CODONS))),
  "Adding the terminator did not add exactly one codon" =
    all(nchar(seqs_ordered) == nchar(seqs) + 3),
  # The stop must not disturb the composition the series is built around: GC3
  # is measured on internal codons, which excludes it by definition.
  "Appending the stop changed the measured GC3" =
    all(abs(map_dbl(seqs_ordered, orf_gc3_pct) - comp_tbl$gc3_pct) < 1e-9)
)
cat("Terminal", ORF_STOP, "appended to all", length(seqs),
    "variants; each ORF now carries exactly one stop, at its end\n")

seq_tbl <- tibble(
  variant    = names(variants),
  gc3_target = targets,
  source     = comp_tbl$source,
  nt         = comp_tbl$cds_length,
  nt_ordered = comp_tbl$cds_length + 3L,
  gc_pct     = comp_tbl$gc_pct,
  gc3_pct    = comp_tbl$gc3_pct,
  gs_linker  = map_chr(variants, "gs"),
  flag       = map_chr(variants, "flag"),
  egfp       = map_chr(variants, "egfp"),
  cds         = unname(seqs),
  cds_ordered = unname(seqs_ordered)
)
write_csv(seq_tbl, file.path(outdir,
                             paste0("12_gc3_series_sequences_", run_tag, ".csv")))
write_csv(comp_tbl, file.path(outdir,
                              paste0("12_gc3_series_composition_", run_tag, ".csv")))
write_csv(drift_tbl, file.path(outdir,
                               paste0("12_gc3_series_usage_drift_", run_tag, ".csv")))
write_csv(part_tbl %>% dplyr::select(-seq),
          file.path(outdir, paste0("12_gc3_series_part_composition_", run_tag, ".csv")))
write_csv(pct_tbl, file.path(outdir,
                             paste0("12_gc3_series_percentiles_vs_231_", run_tag, ".csv")))

cat("Wrote 5 tables to", outdir, "\n")
```
